additional_concerns: The transition expressly preserves existing application processing. Reading this as exclusion from relief is plausible, but a substantive or permanent bar is not established. Neither alternative should be treated as settled.
The introductory immediate-effect wording requires reconciliation with the express 28 November 2025 commencement provision. Neither establishes a universal implementation-date test.
A pending-status fact fixed at commencement does not resolve subsequent approval, withdrawal or resubmission. Change-wide exclusions based on any related application require further support.
Moving commencement or legacy status between scope and result changes OUT_OF_SCOPE versus FALSE outcomes. The candidates answer different questions and are not interchangeable.
The substantive-only question properly excludes application processing. Missing authority for the complete extracted permission claim does not make its narrower substantive formula defective.
The two unbound dependency IDs have no supplied mapping to named authorities. No catalogue match can be inferred.

Actual home-compliance determinations require applicable home-jurisdiction authority; novelty, complexity and possible local policy implications may require SFC guidance. The formulas accept these classifications without establishing them.
Prior-approval relief does not establish notification, filing, post-vetting or overall compliance. The purpose statement does not expressly add an independent home-supervision prerequisite.
